title: How the house edge works
voiceInstructions: Upbeat, natural American English, like a fun explainer creator talking to a friend. Brisk and lively pace with clear numbers. No long pauses.

scenes.say: Ever wonder why sportsbooks keep making money, even when bettors win?
scenes.caption: Ever wonder why sportsbooks keep making money, even when bettors win?

scenes.say: Imagine a game that's exactly fifty-fifty. A fair bet pays one hundred dollars profit on a hundred-dollar wager.
scenes.caption: Imagine a game that’s exactly 50/50. A fair bet pays $100 profit on a $100 wager.

scenes.say: But sportsbooks often charge a hidden price through the odds. Instead of winning a hundred, you might only profit ninety dollars and ninety-one cents.
scenes.caption: But sportsbooks often charge a hidden price through the odds. Instead of winning $100, you might only profit $90.91.

scenes.say: At minus one-ten on both sides, each side has to win about fifty-two point four percent of the time just to break even. In a true fifty-fifty game, neither side can.
scenes.caption: At -110 on both sides, each side has to win about 52.4% of the time just to break even. In a true 50/50 game, neither side can.

scenes.say: Over a hundred fifty-fifty bets of a hundred dollars each, you'd lose about four hundred fifty-five dollars on average.
scenes.caption: Over 100 fifty-fifty bets of $100 each, you’d lose about $455 on average.

scenes.say: That's the house edge. The odds can favor the sportsbook before the game even starts.
scenes.caption: That’s the house edge. The odds can favor the sportsbook before the game even starts.
